text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Thai depositors withdrew almost 30 billion baht from troubled Thai finance companies.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong is "cautiously optimistic" about southern Africa's economic potential.
- Chinese Foreign Ministry denies any attempt made by North Korean agents to enter South Korean consulate in Beijing to get top North Korean defector.
- Property magnate Ng Teng Fong and government-owned Pidemco Land make top bids for three Urban Regional Development condominium plots.
- Mohd Saleh Sulong, business partner of late Yahaya Ahmad, appointed chairman and president of the DRB-Hicom group.
- Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Virawan and Bank of Thailand governor Rerengchai Marakanond deny resigning.
- Housing loan applications on rise at two major local banks.
- Multimedia company Aztech Systems expects new products to power growth.
- Amcol Holdings' bond holders may face long wait to receive payments.
- DBS Bank announces 12.6 percent increase in group net profit to Singapore $669.5 million for 1996.
- Both Keppel Integrated Engineering and sister company Keppel Marine Industries announce poorer profit margins for 1996.
- Keppel Finance announces 15 percent rise in net earnings for last year of Singapore $26.58 million.
